topic: Which Natalie Portman stories are true?

entries.text: During her years at Harvard, there was a phenomenon called "The Natalies" — every underclasswoman with that first name received many emails and phone messages from fans.
Natalie graduated from Harvard in 2003 in the same class as then-friend Jared Kushner. She later attended the Kushner/Ivanka Trump wedding in 2009.
Natalie was the first person born in the 1980s to win the Academy Award for Best Actress, for Black Swan (2010).

trueStory: All 3 are true — The Natalies phenomenon, Kushner classmate, and first 1980s-born Best Actress winner.
closer: All that, and she survived ManBearPig in this movie!
fullText:
Annihilation — the spiritual successor of South Park Season 10, Episode 6, ManBearPig.

We are going to focus on the resplendent Natalie Portman — Excellent in this movie.

Here are 3 stories about Natalie Portman — your job is to tell me which of these 3 stories has the Shimmer of Truth.

Time for the Truthsayer.

1. During her years at Harvard, there was a phenomenon called "The Natalies" wherein every underclasswoman with that first name received MANY emails and phone messages from fans.

2. Natalie graduated from Harvard in 2003 in the same class with then-friend Jared Kushner. She would later attend the Kushner/Ivanka Trump wedding in 2009.

3. Natalie was the first person born in the 1980s to have won the Academy Award for Best Actress (for Black Swan, 2010).

ALL 3 of them are true!

All that, and she survived ManBearPig in this movie!

Here ends the Truthsayer!

topic: Which old website from internet history was real?

entries.text: BabyJessicaWasFake.com (1998) — claimed Baby Jessica falling down a well was a fake stunt to claim oil rights in Midland, TX.
PixelPets (2001) — virtual pet site taken down by the feds after Russian malware was found installing on every computer that accessed it.
CNN OJ Simpson Trial Hub — clip-art links to sub-pages: The Verdict, The Suspect, The Victim, The Murder, The Evidence. Never taken down.

trueStory: The CNN OJ Simpson Trial Hub still exists. Search it and take a walk down memory lane.
closer: Before America forgot what a big-time scandal SHOULD look like.
fullText:
For today's Truthsayer, we are going to look at some less-popular websites from Internet History. 3 old websites — 2 made up, one was real.

#1 — BabyJessicaWasFake.com (1998) — claimed to have incontrovertible proof that Baby Jessica falling down a well in Midland, TX was TOTALLY FAKE.

#2 — PixelPets (2001) — virtual pet site taken down by the feds after Russian malware was discovered.

#3 — CNN OJ Simpson Trial Hub — clip-art links to sub-pages: The Verdict, The Suspect, The Victim, The Murder, The Evidence. Never taken down.

It was the CNN OJ Simpson Trial Hub. Still exists in all its antiquated glory. Before America forgot what a big-time scandal SHOULD look like.

Here ends the Truthsayer.

topic: Which legendary regional video rental store is real?

entries.text: Black Lodge Video in Memphis, TN — Founded 2000, inspired by Twin Peaks. Plush velvet curtains, 30K+ titles on VHS through Laser Disc. Many Twin Peaks cast members have visited.
Screen Sluts in Savannah, GA — Founded by sister of Roger Corman starlet Hazel Court. Largest Corman collection, indoor drive-in with 3 convertibles.
Neon Dreams Video in Portland, OR — Vaporwave aesthetics, 25K titles, hosted a live How Did This Get Made recording in 2023.

trueStory: Black Lodge Video in Memphis is real — recently closed due to financial struggles, owners looking for a smaller location.
closer: Did not see a list of films to check if they carried "Happy-Scrappy Hero Pups" or "Men Alone 2: The K-Y Connection."
fullText:
The Video Rental Store — an antiquated institution from way back in the 1900s.

#1 — Black Lodge Video in Memphis TN — Founded in 2000 inspired by Twin Peaks, with plush velvet curtains. Over 30K films on VHS, DVD, BluRay and Laser Disc. Many Twin Peaks cast members have visited.

#2 — Screen Sluts in Savannah, GA — Founded by the sister of Roger Corman starlet Hazel Court. Largest Corman collection, indoor drive-in with 3 convertibles.

#3 — Neon Dreams Video in Portland, OR — Vaporwave 80s aesthetics, 25K titles. Hosted a live How Did This Get Made recording in 2023.

Black Lodge Video in Memphis is the real video store. Unfortunately it recently closed due to financial struggles. The owners are looking for a smaller location to try again.

Here ends the Truthsayer.

entries.text: The producers originally pitched Jaws 3-D as National Lampoon's Jaws 3, People 0 — a spoof about a studio making a Jaws sequel. Spielberg rejected it and threatened to walk from Universal.
Dennis Quaid distanced himself from this film because he shot it just after coming out of rehab.
Leah Thompson was cast after appearing in a Taco Bell campaign. Her main line was "It hurts my buns."

trueStory: National Lampoon's Jaws 3, People 0 was real — naked Bo Derek, shark-costumed aliens, Joe Dante attached. Spielberg threatened to walk. Zanuck and Brown quit the studio.
closer: When in doubt — stick with the original.
fullText:
Jaws is an unassailable masterpiece. So today we focus on Jaws 3-D.

#1 — Originally pitched as National Lampoon's Jaws 3, People 0 — a spoof where the film opens with Peter Benchley being eaten in his pool. Spielberg rejected it and threatened to walk from Universal. Zanuck and Brown quit the studio.

#2 — Dennis Quaid shot it just after coming out of rehab and hates the way he looked.

#3 — Leah Thompson was cast after a Taco Bell campaign. Her main line was "It hurts my buns."

It wasn't #3 — Leah Thompson was in Burger King commercials. It wasn't #2 — Quaid was aggressively using cocaine in every scene. The true story is #1.

Here ends the Truthsayer!

entries.text: Olivier once filled the dressing room of Sir John Gielgud with chickens.
During a 9-month run of Richard III, Olivier forgot part of the soliloquy and started singing The Sunny Side of the Street.
Alec Guinness and Olivier explored an unknown tunnel under the Old Vic. After several hours, clearly lost, they had to be rescued from deep under the Thames.

trueStory: Guinness wrote about getting lost with Olivier in a tunnel under the Thames. Olivier's willingness to plunge into the dark was characteristic of the actor he was.
closer: The greatest to ever do it.
fullText:
Marathon Man — Laurence Mother Lovin Olivier — my goodness.

#1 — Olivier once filled the dressing room of Sir John Gielgud with chickens.
#2 — During a 9-month run of Richard III, Olivier forgot part of the soliloquy and started singing The Sunny Side of the Street.
#3 — Alec Guinness and Olivier explored a tunnel under the Old Vic. After several hours, clearly lost, they had to be rescued from deep under the Thames.

It was #3. Guinness wrote about the misadventures. Olivier's willingness to plunge into the dark was characteristic of the actor he was. The greatest to ever do it.

Here ends the Truthsayer.

fullText:

Here ends the Truthsayer!

topic: Which 1967 Spider-Man cartoon facts are true?

entries.text: Spider-Man was voiced by Canadian character actor Paul Soles who also voiced Hermey the Elf in the 1964 claymation classic Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer.
Spider-Man is often heard saying "Wallopin' websnappers" in this show — the expression was created for the cartoon.
The spider on Spider-Man's costume only had 6 legs in Season 1 due to budget constraints.

trueStory: All 3 true. Paul Soles voiced both Spidey and Hermey the Elf. The 6-leg spider was corrected in Season 2 but reused Season 1 animation still had the error.
closer: Look out! Here comes the Truthsayer!
fullText:
SpiderVerse (both films) sit atop the Spider Canon for me. So today we focus on a version not on top — the 1967 Saturday morning cartoon.

#1 — Spider-Man was voiced by Paul Soles who also voiced Hermey the Elf in Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer.
#2 — Spider-Man is often heard saying "Wallopin' websnappers" — created for the cartoon.
#3 — The spider on Spider-Man's costume only had 6 legs in Season 1.

Wallopin' Websnappers! ALL Three were true! Paul Soles was 37 when he did the voice. The 6-leg error was corrected in Season 2 but reused Season 1 animation still had it.

Look out! Here comes the Truthsayer!

topic: True origin story of the turtleneck

entries.text: Turtleneck type garments date back to the 15th century, designed to protect the necks of Knights wearing chainmail.
The Turtleneck was so associated with leftist academics that the US Navy banned them for off-duty officers in 1902.
In 1971, John V. Tunney became the first Senator to wear a turtleneck on the Senate floor. It caused quite a scene.

trueStory: Turtleneck-style garments date to the 15th century — designed to protect knights' necks from chainmail chafing.
closer: Chainmail's gotta chafe, y'all. NORMALIZE COLORECTAL HEALTHCARE y'all!
fullText:
Currently doing colonoscopy prep, so we gotta make this quick.

No one has ever worn a Turtleneck as well as Steve McQueen in this movie.

#1 — Turtleneck garments date back to the 15th century, designed to protect the necks of Knights wearing chainmail.
#2 — The US Navy banned them for off-duty officers in 1902.
#3 — In 1971, John V. Tunney became the first Senator to wear a turtleneck on the Senate floor.

It was the Knights and Chainmail Origin story. Chainmail's gotta chafe, y'all.

NORMALIZE COLORECTAL HEALTHCARE y'all!

Here ends the Truthsayer.

entries.text: Pleasance was a radio operator on British Bombers in WW2. Shot down in 1944, he organized a theater company in the POW camp — performing The Petrified Forest opposite a 6'1" Canadian in the Bette Davis role.
As Blofeld in You Only Live Twice, Pleasance was allergic to cats and needed antihistamine injections to perform scenes with the iconic white Turkish Angora.
Pleasance became unlikely friends with Isaac Hayes on Escape from New York. They kept correspondence until Donald's death in 1995. Hayes performed Amazing Grace at the funeral.

trueStory: Pleasance really was an RAF POW. One of the few Great Escape stars who had actually been a prisoner of war — initially told to keep his opinions to himself until Sturges learned the truth.
fullText:
For the Halloween Truthsayer — Donald Pleasance, Dr Sam Loomis.

#1 — Pleasance was a radio operator on British Bombers in WW2. Shot down in 1944, organized a theater company in the POW camp.
#2 — As Blofeld, Pleasance was allergic to cats and needed antihistamine injections.
#3 — Unlikely friends with Isaac Hayes on Escape from New York. Hayes performed Amazing Grace at Pleasance's funeral.

It was #1. Pleasance was one of the few Great Escape stars who had actually been a POW. When he offered advice to director Sturges he was told to keep his opinions to himself — until Sturges learned the truth.

Here ends the Truthsayer.
